accept.description: Mark findings of layout, ergonomics, electrical or plumbing as looked at, by the key the review gives: accept=[[key, reason]] — they stay in their review with the reason and stop counting (score, pendencies, dry runs); an empty reason takes one back. prune=true drops every acceptance whose finding is gone (the reviews list them as orphaned). One undoable step. Reply ok, with accepted and removed counts; read the review again to see it.
`[[key, reason]]`, key as the review names it (`layout`, ergonomics, electrical, plumbing): it keeps showing there with the reason and stops counting. An empty reason takes it back

prune.description: Drop every acceptance whose finding is gone — the `orphaned` the reviews list — from all of them at once

accept.name: accept
accept.title: Accept findings

annotations.description: Plan annotations, read. stale=true lists what no longer matches: notes whose numbers differ from their piece, piece names whose sizes (`módulo 70 cm`, `80 × 60`) differ, dimensions whose anchor is gone, and unanchored ones left with an end in the air near a face — rows [id, written, measured, against, text]; checked {dims, dims_unanchored, labels, names} counts what was compared (nothing checked is not a clean plan), and unverified [[id, text]] lists sizes nothing can confirm. It is the check after moving geometry. A note is tied to its piece with update(id=t1, about=f5). q=<text> searches label text on every storey, q=re:<pattern> by regex. With neither, answers the schedule {dims,refs,details,legend,rooms:[[room,[[tag,name,w,d,h,brand?,model?,url?]]]]}. `edit_annotations` switches modes, ties dimensions and bakes chains; brand, model and url go on pieces with `update`.

q.description: Search label text, accent- and case-insensitive, e.g. `porta`; or `re:<pattern>` for a regular expression

stale.description: Dimensions and notes that no longer match the drawing: rows [id, written, measured, against, text]

annotations.name: annotations
annotations.title: Read dimensions, tags and notes

arrange.description: Arrange elements in one undo step. array {ids,n,dx,dy,dz} adds n copies stepping by dx/dy/dz cm (rafters, columns); align {ids,axis,edge:low|middle|high,value} lines pieces up by an edge — backs on one line, fronts on another — instead of by centers you work out yourself; distribute {ids,axis,gap?} sets them side by side in the order given, from where the first one is (a run of joinery); flip {ids} turns a piece back to front, rebuilding what is inside it (mirror only swaps left and right and leaves the front where it was); rotate {ids,angle clockwise,about?,copy?}; mirror {ids,a,b,copy?} across the line a-b; group {ids,name?} joins pieces into one box that moves/hides together, ungroup {ids:[group]}; front/back {ids} draws rooms or pieces on top/underneath (pool over deck, rug under sofa). Returns new ids.

a.description: mirror: the first point of the mirror line

about.description: rotate: pivot `[x,y]` (default the center of the elements)

action.description: What to do; `array` makes copies in a row

b.description: mirror: the second point of the mirror line

copy.description: rotate/mirror: keep the originals and transform a copy

dx.description: array: step per copy along x, cm

dy.description: array: step per copy along y, cm

dz.description: array: step per copy upwards, cm (furniture and labels)

edge.description: align: which edge to line up — `low` (left, or top of the plan), `middle`, `high`

gap.description: distribute: centimeters between one piece and the next (default 0)

ids.description: The elements to act on (ungroup: the group)

value.description: align: the coordinate, cm, to put that edge on

arrange.name: arrange
arrange.title: Copy, align and group

background.description: Walls detected in the scanned plan under the drawing (`edit_background` action=set puts it there): thick dark or gray bands across or down the image become walls, colored areas (lawn, plants, furniture) are ignored, and pieces split by doors or windows up to max_gap join; region limits the search. Returns rows [[x1,y1],[x2,y2],t] in plan cm without drawing; `edit_background` action=trace creates them. Check with `render_plan` bg=0.5.

max_gap.description: Doors and windows up to this wide don't split a wall, cm (default 130)

region.description: Only this part of the plan `[x0, y0, x1, y1]` cm

threshold.description: Luminance 0..255 below which a gray pixel is ink (default 128; raise it for light gray walls)

background.name: background
background.title: Find walls in a scan

cabinet_run.description: Fill a wall with cabinets sized for it: measures the free stretches between corners, doors, windows, fridge and stove, splits each into even modules (30-90 cm, no useless leftovers; 15-30 cm pull-outs, fillers under 15; the defaults target=60 max=90 sink_w=80 cooktop_w=60 are the nominal widths of EN 1116, which is what appliances and hardware are made for — bespoke widths in between are fine for a run that receives none), drawer unit beside the stove, countertop on base rows, cabinet over the fridge and hood gap on wall rows, wardrobes (hanging rails, shelves, drawers) on tall rows facing bedrooms; p.sink/p.cooktop place those cabinets and cutouts. Replaces the cabinets already there (keep ids stay). Reply {modules:[[id,role,from,w]],removed,notes}; dry plans only. Change one module afterwards with joinery id.

from.description: Stretch to fill, cm from the wall start (default: all of it)

keep.description: Cabinets on that wall that stay as they are

near.description: Or a piece against the wall (`f12`, the fridge): its nearest wall, on its side

p.description: Flat choices, all optional: row base|wall|tall, h, d, elev, t (mm), front, color [r,g,b], handle bar|profile|knob|cava|none (bar), `handle_color` [r,g,b] or "#hex", drawers (drawer units), max (widest module, 90), target (60), top (base countertop, true), `top_material`, sink / cooktop (center cm along the wall: cabinet under it and the countertop cutout), `sink_w` (80), `cooktop_w` (60), interior shelves|hanging|wardrobe (tall rows; wardrobe by default facing a bedroom)

room.description: Room the fronts face (default: the side toward the middle of the house)

to.description: Where the run ends, cm from the wall start (default: the wall's end)

wall.description: Wall whose face gets the cabinets

cabinet_run.name: cabinet_run
cabinet_run.title: Fill a wall with cabinets

cameras.description: Stored points of view: {active: visitor|aerial, rows [i,name,x,y,z,yaw,pitch,fov]}, cm and degrees. Change them with edit_cameras.
cameras.name: cameras
cameras.title: List points of view

catalog.description: Find catalog items: rows [id,name,w,d,h,front?] in cm. front, when the item has one, is `wall|free <front>/<back>`: every model is built with that front on its local +y (at angle 0 it looks down the plan), `wall` means its back belongs on a wall (bed headboard, wardrobe back, toilet cistern) and `free` that it stands anywhere (armchair, chair); no front means any angle is right. scope=project lists what this plan already uses instead — catalog id or imported model, with how many there are and one id to copy from, narrowed by q over the entry and its pieces' names — which is how a new piece matches the drawing rather than reintroducing a generic one.

q.description: Search words (Portuguese or English), e.g. `cama casal`

scope.description: `project` lists what this plan already uses — imported models included — instead of the catalog, so a new piece can match what is there rather than reintroduce a generic one

catalog.name: catalog
catalog.title: Search the furniture catalog

create.description: Create walls (polylines; hs = height per point for gables), rooms (pts, or at=[x,y] to detect from walls; ceiling_flat=false follows wall profiles instead of the default flat ceiling), dims (a+b or wall id), labels, roofs (rectangle pts, gable|shed, pitch or ridge_h, eave h, overhang, gables=true closes the ends, skylights [{at,w,d}] cut glazed openings) and solids (pts outline raised by h at elev: slabs/mezzanines of any shape; or profile [[u,z]] swept from a to b: gables, ramps) in one atomic step.

a.description: Start of a free dimension, `[x,y]` cm

b.description: End of a free dimension, `[x,y]` cm

chain.description: With `wall`: one dimension per wall piece and opening along the face

elev.description: With `in3d`: height of the line above the floor, cm

off.description: Offset cm from the measured line (default 40 for walls; a/b: left of a→b is positive)

pitch.description: With `in3d`: tilt around its line, degrees (90 = offset upwards)

room.description: Clear width and depth of a room, e.g. `r5` (two dimensions)

side.description: `out` (outer face, default for chains), `in` (inner face) or `axis` (default)

wall.description: Measure a wall: `side` picks the line, `chain` splits at openings

pitch.description: Show in 3D tilted this much: 0 lying on the floor, 90 standing

closed.description: Join the last point back to the first

divider.description: Room divider: splits an open space into rooms without a wall (dashed)

gables.description: Also close the gable ends with sloping walls

h.description: Eave height above the storey floor, cm (default 250)

kind.description: Default `gable` (steep = A-frame); `shed` rises from the pts[0]→pts[1] side

pitch.description: Slope in degrees (default 30), unless `ridge_h` is given

pts.description: Rectangle corners in order; the ridge runs along pts[0]→pts[1]

ridge_h.description: Ridge (gable) or high side (shed) height above the floor, cm

skylights.description: Glazed roof openings: center `at`, `w` along the ridge, `d` across, cm

at.description: A point inside a space enclosed by walls (auto-detects the polygon)

ceiling_flat.description: Flat ceiling at storey height (default) or following wall profiles (false)

pts.description: Floor polygon; or omit and give `at`

room_use.description: Declared room program, independent of name; auto restores inference

RoomUse.description: Declared room program; `auto` infers it from the name and equipment

a.description: With `profile`: where the sweep starts, `[x,y]` cm

b.description: With `profile`: where the sweep ends, `[x,y]` cm

elev.description: Outline bottom above the floor cm (default 0)

profile.description: Instead of `pts`: cross-section `[[u,z],…]` cm swept from `a` to `b` (+u is +x when a→b goes down the plan; z above the floor)

arc.description: Arc extent in degrees applied to every segment (positive bulges left)

closed.description: Join the last point back to the first

hs.description: Height cm at each point, for sloping walls and gables (overrides `h`)

pts.description: Polyline vertices; N points make N-1 joined walls

sides.description: Finish on both sides, e.g. `#f2efe6` or `subway 20x10`

type.description: Wall type id, e.g. `drywall-95`; sets the thickness unless `t` is given

dims.description: Dimension lines: between two points, along a wall, or across a room

exact.description: Keep wall ends as given; no snap onto nearby walls

polylines.description: Free lines: annotations, arrows, electrical or plumbing runs

px.description: Points are background-image pixels; lengths stay in cm

roofs.description: Pitched roofs over a rectangle, as one group of panels

rooms.description: Rooms: an outline of points, or `at` inside closed walls

solids.description: Solids: outlines raised by `h` (slabs) or sections swept `a`→`b` (gables, ramps)

v.description: Plan version (tab) to write to; switches to it first

walls.description: Walls, each a chain of points joined corner to corner

create.name: create
create.title: Draw walls, rooms and more

cut_list.description: Cut list of joinery builds, and of groups drawn by hand: each part of a drawn group up to 50 mm thick is a board at the size it was drawn (board is its finish and thickness, no edge banding), the groups are named in drawn and the parts that are not boards in skipped [[id,name]]. Rows [part,board,qty,length,width,thickness mm,edge long+short,cutouts [x,y,w,d] mm?] merged by size, hardware, sheets per board. export what=cut_list writes it as .csv, or .dxf/.svg (boards laid out on sheets). sources names the panel standards behind the boards: MDF is a dry-process fibreboard (NBR 15316), MDP a particleboard of 551 to 750 kg/m³ that holds screws better (NBR 14810).

ids.description: Build or drawn group ids (default: every build and drawn group on this storey)

cut_list.name: cut_list
cut_list.title: Cut list

delete.description: Delete (remove) walls, rooms, pieces or any element by id, atomically. Labels left pointing at a deleted piece — about it, or standing on it — are named in the reply as labels_left [[id, text]], since an index code over what is now another piece is found by nobody; labels=true deletes them in the same step.

ids.description: The elements to delete: walls, rooms, pieces, dimensions, labels, lines

labels.description: Also delete the labels left pointing at the deleted pieces

delete.name: delete
delete.title: Delete elements

disciplines.description: Electrical and plumbing projects and plan layers over the plan. active (default): {active, hidden, layers {key:{pieces, hidden}}} — the discipline new symbols go to, what is hidden, and the layers (lighting, appliances, joinery); home gives each piece its plan_layer. quantities: {electrical:[[kind,count,names?]], plumbing:[...], lines_cm:{...}} — grouped by catalog kind (every low outlet together), with the names of the points as the detail. Change what is shown with edit_disciplines.
disciplines.name: disciplines
disciplines.title: Show what the plan displays

edit_annotations.description: Change the plan annotations. anchor=true ties every straight dimension to what its ends touch now, so it is measured again on every change instead of drifting (tie them while the numbers are right); one already off its face is not tied and comes back in left [[id, written, measured, near]], and one whose anchor died with a deleted piece is tied again or released. Switch dims (dimension chains), refs (the room reference schedule, whose tags stay with their pieces; renumber=true numbers them again in reading order), details (brand/model/link in refs) and legend (symbols with counts): a switch answers with the modes, changed, and what it shows — chains [[from,to,cm]] for dims, symbols {discipline:[[name,count]]} for legend; refs=true returns the schedule {dims,refs,details,legend,rooms:[[room,[[tag,name,w,d,h,brand?,model?,url?]]]]}. bake=true turns the automatic chains into editable dimensions (ids returned). `annotations` reads them.

anchor.description: Tie every straight dimension to what its ends touch right now, so from here on they follow the drawing. Run it while the numbers are right

bake.description: Convert the automatic dimension chains into editable dimensions

details.description: Include brand, model and link in references (`reference_details`)

dims.description: Show engineering dimension chains (`auto_dimensions` in the project JSON)

legend.description: Legend of electrical/plumbing symbols with counts

refs.description: Show the room reference schedule and tags (`references` in the JSON)

renumber.description: Number the schedule again in reading order, closing the gaps pieces left behind. Numbers are otherwise kept by each piece for good

edit_annotations.name: edit_annotations
edit_annotations.title: Change dimensions and tags

annotations.title: Set or trace a scanned plan

edit_background.description: Put a scanned plan under the drawing at real scale, or turn it into walls. set {path, then cm_per_px (+cm_per_px_y), calibrate {a,b px, cm} or calibrations [{a,b,cm}…] to fit X/Y scales; angle (clockwise °); offset, opacity, visible; clear=true removes it}. trace {threshold?, min_len?, t_min?, t_max?, max_gap?, region?, h?} creates, in one undo step, the walls `background` detects with the same options, on the image set puts there. Check with `render_plan` bg=0.5.

action.description: What to do with the scanned plan

angle.description: For `set`: clockwise turn of the image, degrees

calibrate.description: For `set`: two pixels with a known real distance, `{a, b, cm}`

calibrations.description: For `set`: several known distances, fitting X and Y scales apart

cm_per_px.description: For `set`: the scale, cm per image pixel

cm_per_px_y.description: For `set`: the vertical scale, when it differs

max_gap.description: For `trace`: doors and windows up to this wide don't split a wall, cm (default 130)

offset.description: For `set`: plan position cm of the image's top-left corner

opacity.description: For `set`: how opaque the image is drawn, 0..1

path.description: For `set`: image file (png/jpg/webp/bmp); required when there is no background yet

region.description: For `trace`: only this part of the plan `[x0, y0, x1, y1]` cm

threshold.description: For `trace`: luminance 0..255 below which a gray pixel is ink (default 128)

visible.description: For `set`: show or hide the image without removing it

edit_background.name: edit_background
edit_background.title: Set or trace a scanned plan

edit_cameras.description: Change the points of view. view {i} shows stored view i in the 3D window; aerial returns to the orbit view; store {name?,x?,y?,z?,yaw?,pitch?,fov?,look_at?:[x,y,z]} saves one (missing values from the visitor; yaw 0 looks toward +y/plan bottom, 90 toward -x; pitch positive looks down); delete {i}. cm and degrees. The list is the cameras tool.

action.description: What to do with the points of view

look_at.description: For `store`: point `[x,y,z]` cm to look at (sets yaw and pitch)

name.description: For `store`: the view's name (default "Ponto de vista N")

x.description: Eye position on the plan, cm

y.description: Eye position on the plan, cm (y grows down)

yaw.description: Direction the eye looks, degrees clockwise on the plan

edit_cameras.name: edit_cameras
edit_cameras.title: Change points of view

edit_disciplines.description: Change what the plan shows. select {d: electrical|plumbing|architecture}: new symbols (catalog cat electrical/plumbing) and lines go there and the rest is dimmed; select architecture hides the electrical and plumbing projects (show brings one back); select a project shows it with the architecture dimmed. show/hide {d}, where d can also be a layer of the plan — lighting (lamps, spots, LED), appliances (fridge, stove, oven, hood, washer…) or joinery (cabinets, wardrobes, countertops): hidden from the plan, its exports and the 3D. The 3D follows the plan unless show_all_3d=true, which makes it show everything. Pieces are in a layer by what they are; update(layer=lighting|appliances|joinery|none) overrides it. What is shown now is the disciplines tool.

d.description: `electrical`, `plumbing` or `architecture`; for show/hide also a plan layer: `lighting`, `appliances` or `joinery`

show_all_3d.description: Whether the 3D shows everything (true) or hides what the plan hides (false). Applies with any action

edit_disciplines.name: edit_disciplines
edit_disciplines.title: Show or hide disciplines

edit_electrical.description: Change the electrical and telecom project (`electrical` reads it); each action is one undoable step. assign {ids, circuit, va?}, or circuits {"C1": [ids], …} for the whole division, writes circuits, power and volts (127|220; a 220 V outlet makes its circuit 220 V) on points; on automation points it takes standby_w, on a dimmer max_w, on a panel modules. voltage {volts?, short_ka?, earthing?}. cable {kind, pts} draws a run by hand (with ids or circuit instead of pts it is a route). route {kind, ids? | circuit?, via?: ceiling|floor|wall|tape, cat?, from?} lays the run as it is built, from the nearest panel along and inside the walls, replacing the earlier run of the circuit, and answers {via, suggested, length_m, by_premise_m, bends, materials: [[item, qty, unit]]}; without via it takes the cheapest premise that can be built. via=tape is surface flat wiring, power only (`rules` topic=electrical). wifi {ids, standard?, poe?, uplink?, bands?} writes those on access points.

action.description: `assign` puts `ids` on `circuit` (empty takes them off), `va` sets their power; `voltage` is the supply, 127 or 220 V

band.description: For `wifi`: the band the suggestion aims at, `2.4`, `5` (default) or `6`

bands.description: For `wifi`: the bands they radiate when fewer than their generation's, e.g. `2.4,5` for a dual-band Wi-Fi 7

circuits.description: For `assign`: the whole division at once, `{"C1": [ids], "C2": [ids]}`, in one undoable step

from.description: For `route`: the panel it starts from; default the nearest of its kind

kind.description: For `cable` and `route`: what the run carries

max_w.description: For `assign` on a dimmer: the most lighting it takes, W

modules.description: For `assign` on a distribution panel: the DIN modules it holds

poe.description: For `wifi`: whether `ids` are fed by their data cable (`PoE`)

short_ka.description: For `voltage`: the presumed short-circuit current at the delivery point, kA, as the utility informs it

standard.description: For `wifi`: the access points' standard, `wifi5`, `wifi6`, `wifi6e` or `wifi7`, written on `ids`

standby_w.description: For `assign` on automation points: standby consumption, W

uplink.description: For `wifi`: the access points' wired uplink, Gbps (1, 2.5, 5, 10)

va.description: Power per point, VA, instead of the norm's default

via.description: For `route`: where the run passes, `ceiling` (slab, dropping in the walls), `floor` or `wall`. Omitted: the cheapest that can be built

volts.description: Supply voltage, V; with `assign`, the points' own, 127 or 220

edit_electrical.name: edit_electrical
edit_electrical.title: Change the electrical project

edit_estimate.description: Change the project's estimate. add_line {title, unit_price, quantity?, unit?, currency?, vat_included?, shop?, note?}: a line of your own (labour, delivery, glue, primer); remove_line {line}; save {name?}: keep the estimate as it is now, never changed after; remove_saved {saved}: delete a saved one. Reply: the line, or the saved estimate with its totals. estimate reads it.

action.description: `add_line` adds a line of your own; `remove_line` takes one off; `save` keeps the estimate as it is now; `remove_saved` deletes a saved one

line.description: For `remove_line`: the line's id, as estimate lists it

name.description: For `save`: the name it is kept under; default the date and time

note.description: For `add_line`: a remark kept with the line

saved.description: For `remove_saved`: the saved estimate's name or id

shop.description: For `add_line`: who it is bought from or paid to

title.description: For `add_line`: what it is, e.g. `Tiling labour`, `Delivery`, `Tile adhesive 25 kg`

unit.description: For `add_line`: what the quantity counts, e.g. `hour`; default `item`

unit_price.description: For `add_line`: the price of one, as text, e.g. `"45.00"`

vat_included.description: For `add_line`: whether the price includes VAT; unsaid, its totals are apart from both

edit_estimate.name: edit_estimate
edit_estimate.title: Change the estimate

edit_finishes.description: Put a shop product (tile, laminate, paint, wallpaper) on a room's floor or ceiling or a wall side, or take it off. assign {surface, product, band?, coats?, waste?, mat?}: band [from,to] cm splits a wall side (tile below, paint above); mat sets the look in the same step. remove {surface, band?}. One undo step. finishes lists them.

action.description: `assign` puts a product on a surface, replacing the one on the same band; `remove` takes it off

band.description: Height on a wall side, `[from, to]` cm above the floor (default all of it); `remove` without it clears the whole surface

mat.description: For `assign`: the surface's look, as `update` takes it (`#rrggbb`, `tiles #ffffff 30x60`, `img:…`). Hosted, a whole surface without it takes the product's: its swatch at its size, or its colour

product.description: For `assign`: the hosted service's product id

surface.description: `r3:floor`, `r3:ceiling`, `w5:left` or `w5:right` (sides as seen walking from the wall's a to b)

waste.description: For `assign`: waste %, bought on top for cuts and breakage

edit_finishes.name: edit_finishes
edit_finishes.title: Put products on surfaces

edit_history.description: Undo, redo, or name where the plan is now and come back to it. undo and redo step through changes, whoever made them, and the reply names what changed. checkpoint {label} remembers this point; revert {label} undoes back down to it, keeping every id — which duplicating a version cannot do, since a copy renumbers. A checkpoint lives with the project and survives saving; `history` lists them.
edit_history.name: edit_history
edit_history.title: Undo, redo, checkpoints

edit_home.description: Rename the project, set or remove project properties (properties {key: value|null}, or a storey's with level), set the compass (north), set the city whose building code applies (city=sao-paulo), and say who lives there (people {occupants, children, elderly, wheelchair, stature cm, scope}). City and people belong to the project: `ergonomics`, `layout` and every dry run then weigh the same rules for the same people, so a change can be tested against the score it moves.

People.description: Who lives there, as far as this call says; the rest is the project's

children.description: Of them, children (sleep in single beds or cribs)

city.description: City whose building code applies for this call only, e.g. `sao-paulo`; `edit_home(city=…)` keeps it with the project

scope.description: Disciplines included in the score. Architecture always counts; excluded findings remain visible

stature.description: Height of the main cook, cm, to size the countertop (default 165)

wheelchair.description: Someone uses a wheelchair: NBR 9050 turning space, doors and reach

ReviewScope.description: Disciplines included in the habitability score. Architecture is always included; other findings remain visible even when outside the score

electrical.description: Count electrical findings in the score (default true)

plumbing.description: Count plumbing findings in the score (default true)

city.description: City whose building code applies, e.g. `sao-paulo`; `""` clears it. Kept with the project, so `ergonomics`, `layout` and every dry run weigh the same municipal rules

compass_at.description: Where the compass sits on the plan, `[x,y]` cm

country.description: Country whose standards apply, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2: `br`, `us`, `de`; `""` clears it. It decides which sources oblige and which only inform — a Brazilian standard is a reference in Florida, and the IRC is a reference here. A city we hold implies its country, so this is for saying where a project is when no code was picked

north.description: Clockwise degrees from plan up to north

people.description: Who lives there — occupants, children, elderly, wheelchair, stature cm, scope — kept with the project: ergonomics and every dry run then score for them. What is left out stays as it was

properties.description: Project properties to set, `{key: "value"}`, or remove, `{key: null}` — what an import leaves behind (window sizes, panel dividers, ids of the program it came from). With `level`, that storey's instead

region.description: State or province whose code applies: `sp`, `fl`; `""` clears it. In the United States it is the state that adopts a building code, so it matters as much as the country there

edit_home.name: edit_home
edit_home.title: Project settings

edit_levels.description: Change the storeys. add {name?,h?,elev?} adds one on top (or at elev cm) and selects it; select {id}; delete {id} removes it and its content. update {id, elev?|h?|name?|reference?}: elev raises a storey with its walls, floors and openings (houses on stilts); reference=true marks it a tracing layer (imported plan, older version) that checks and ergonomics skip, which is what you want when two storeys share an elevation. Other tools act on the selected storey. The list is the levels tool.

action.description: What to do with the storeys

elev.description: Floor elevation cm for `add` and `update` (e.g. a house on stilts)

reference.description: Mark the storey as a reference layer: a traced plan, a scan, an earlier version. Its content is drawing, not building, so layout checks and ergonomics leave it alone even when it sits at the same elevation as the storey being designed

edit_levels.name: edit_levels
edit_levels.title: Change storeys

edit_library.description: Publish to the asset library: action=publish keeps a piece's model file — with its companion files, reference pictures, measured sizes, unit, box, brand and source link — as the next version of name, with notes on what changed and fidelity (what was estimated). A version never changes after; library lists them.

action.description: `publish`: the piece's model as the next version of `name`

fidelity.description: publish: how far it can be trusted (what was estimated, what was measured)

id.description: publish: the piece whose model, photos, measurements and unit are kept, e.g. `f12`

name.description: publish: the entry, lowercase letters, digits, - and _ (e.g. `oak-armchair`)

notes.description: publish: what changed in this version

feedback.description: Report to the developers what a tool could do better, as it happens: a reply that answered less than was asked, a detour, a wrong conclusion reached before the right one, a fix that would distort the plan, something missing. It is a report the fix will be made from, so give the whole case — a vague note gets fixed in a way that breaks what already works. Every part is required: goal (the task and the situation: pieces, rooms, numbers), tried (the exact call with arguments), got (the literal reply), expected (what was true and how you found out), cost (the workaround, extra calls, wrong conclusion), would_help (the concrete change), must_keep (what works today and must not get worse with that change; "none known" is an answer). kind friction|bug|idea, tool. Kept on this machine and, while the user's telemetry is on, sent to the project. Reply {kept, sent}; then carry on with the task.

must_keep.description: What works today and must keep working with that change — the cases where the current behaviour is right. "none known" is an answer

render_3d.description: PNG of the home in 3D (software render with outlines, no GPU needed). view: front|back|left|right|top orthographic elevations — front looks from the plan's bottom edge (large y) toward y=0, back from y=0 toward large y, left from x=0, right from large x; cut=cm makes a section keeping only what is beyond that plane from the viewer (front cut=200 keeps y<200, so the wall at y=0 stays as the backdrop; to remove it look from back), aerial (default; frames the whole building; yaw degrees: 0 from east/+x, 90 from south/plan bottom (default 60); pitch down; zoom >1 farther), visitor (current visitor camera) or cam=i (stored point of view). walls=cutaway drops the walls between the eye and a room to 40 cm, walls=down drops them all; either hides ceilings, roofs and the doors, windows and wall pieces of lowered walls, to see the furniture from the side. piece=<id> draws it alone, seen from its own side (view; aerial is three-quarter), framed the same wherever it stands; part=<name> frames one part of its model; ref=i puts its reference photo beside it, from the photo's side. Keep w/h small.

Returns PNG. One runs at a time, on at most half the cores (4): threads lowers that, max_s stops it past a deadline, estimate=true answers the budget and the work (pixels, rays, triangles, memory) without rendering, cancel=true stops the one running (sessions shows it).

update.description: Change fields of elements by id; each field applies only to the kinds that have it (furniture mat/opacity/pitch, wall h_end, room auto/ceiling_flat, polyline divider). A part of a group takes name, brand, model_name and url on its own; its size and place belong to the group. anchor on a resize holds one face still instead of growing around the center; stretch=[part ids] on a group resize grows only those parts and moves the rest along (uprights keep 5.8 cm while the opening grows). dry=true answers what it would do without writing: changed fields, clearances around each piece it touches (negative: cm it would sit inside what it faces), issues_resolved/issues_new [{ids, kind, extent|cm|over}] with the kinds `layout` gives, and issues_changed (extent_was); dry="summary" leaves out the parts a group rebuilds. Otherwise the reply names what changed. rename {pattern, to, what} renames in bulk by a regex (Rust syntax, `(?i)` for any case, `$1` in to) in one step; with dry it lists them first.
